_README: Exceptions for check-table-usage.mjs. Every entry needs a reason.
The gate FAILS only on `twins` — a pair of near-identical tables where one is
written and the other read. readOnly / writeOnly are informational (shown with
--verbose) and listed here so the output stays readable and the intentional
cases are stated once instead of re-argued every run.
KNOWN LIMITATION of the scanner: it matches `.from('t')` chains only. A table
read through a PostgREST nested embed — `products ( combo_items ( ... ) )` —
is invisible to it and will look write-only. That is why combo_items is here.

readOnly.reason: Reference data. Seeded by migration and by 59_backfill_default_role_permissions. The app never writes it.
Reference data. Rows are created in the admin portal by hand / by migration, never by application code.
Written exclusively by the apply_credit_transaction RPC, which the scanner cannot see. Reading it in credit.ts is correct.
Written by the till via /api/sync/push, which resolves the table name dynamically. reports.ts:286 reads it. Confirm this stays true if the sync route is ever refactored.

writeOnly.reason: Append-only audit. Read by the admin portal UI over PostgREST directly, not through apps/*/src.
Append-only audit trail for unit_cost changes. No reader yet by design.
Written on clock in/out; the timesheet report aggregates it via an RPC rather than a .from() chain.
SCANNER LIMITATION, not a finding. Read through the nested embed products(combo_items(...)) in combos.ts and the POS catalogue fetch.
SCANNER LIMITATION. Read via the goods_received_notes(grn_items(...)) embed in stock.ts.
SCANNER LIMITATION. Read via the stock_transfers(stock_transfer_items(...)) embed in stock.ts.
Written on each onboarding step; read by the dashboard through the /api/onboarding response rather than a direct .from().
